label: 2026-11-17h — daily-config baseline of the Resolve agentic suite, fixtures rebuilt (two passes: one with a disclosed context deviation, one clean)
question: After the 2026-11-17g wave's operator-side fixture flaws voided three cells per arm, what is the honest measured ceiling of the daily config (no proxy, engine default effort) on the seven-brief suite?
answer: 21/21 in the clean pass. The ceiling of this suite is not currently limited by the agent: every brief, including the two that 17g could not score (T8 comp attach, F2 grade survival), is achievable through the MCP surface.
task_set: seven briefs (T1 read-only probe, T2 marker, T3 ripple insert, T7 render loop, T8 Fusion comp attach, F1 slip-with-loss-disclosure, F2 ripple-after-transition) x 3 trials = 21 sessions per pass, 42 sessions total

build.agent_harness: opencode v2.3.0 (version logged per session, no drift in either pass)
build.engine: Splash 1.7.0 local, daily config — supervisor arg line + startup banner captured in each pass's engine_config.json (config on disk is not proof)
build.reasoning_effort: engine default; OpenCode sends none (no proxy in either pass — the 17g A/B is closed)
build.resolve: DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.2, headless via the community MCP server
build.community_mcp_server: 5.3.1 — src/server.py sha256 362e6a80944b9817013292e1956569a7686c761c4d5c727d6834a0b8b3af810d, 341 registered tool names, 662 action branches (fingerprint: bench/resolve-agentic/mcp-fingerprint-pre5.3.3.json)

pass1_baseline-2026-11-17h.deviation: run with --keep-agents: the operator's global AGENTS.md was present in every trial context (seal probe 9, 2026-11-16f, proves both global and per-cwd AGENTS.md are injected). pass2_baseline-2026-11-17h2.role: the comparable/ceiling pass, and the control for pass 1's context deviation

cost_table.note: cost_usd 0.0 throughout: local engine, no metered API

surface_scan.method: seal_surface_scan.py over archived transcripts; separates completed calls by server and counts mangled-name attempts separately (a mangled name reaches no server, so it is harness friction, not a breach)
surface_scan.pass1_context_note: pass 1's heavier scripting-bridge use concentrated in the struggling trials (T7r3: 36 bridge vs 1 community, still PASS; T8r2: 17 vs 0, PASS via snapshot; T2r1: reached neither)

product_behaviour_measured.f2_ripple_after_transition: grade AND link of the shifted clip are destroyed in 6/6 trials across both passes; every trial disclosed both. Expectation for future F2 specs: expect_lost = [link, grade]. The transition itself always survives (it sits before the insert point).
product_behaviour_measured.f1_slip: speed, retime and audio-in-step destroyed as the MCP's own not_carried list predicts; grade/transform/crop preserved; link also destroyed (17h added this to the observed set, though F1's spec does not track it).
product_behaviour_measured.t8_comp_survival: 6/6 trials read comp_count 1 at their in-trial snapshot AND 6/6 still read 1 post-wave, through both creation paths (MCP add_comp and scripting bridge). This DISPROVES the strong form of the 17g reading (six trials 1 in-wave, 0 after grading): survival across project close/load is not deterministic in either direction. The resolve-ai-workflow daily rule now says re-verify after any project switch, never assume. Grading still uses the in-trial snapshot.
product_behaviour_measured.tool_name_mangling: ~57-58 failed attempts per pass at hyphen-separated MCP tool names (davinci-resolve-media_pool instead of davinci-resolve_media_pool). Harmless everywhere except pass 1's T2r1, where it was total. Candidate harness fix for a future wave: alias or hint the naming convention in the brief.

fixtures_note: one scratch project per pass (the 17g two-arm design raced on Resolve's host-global current project; single project + sequential trials removes the class). MCP auto-versioning creates <timeline>_archived_vNN copies on destructive ops: deleted before sealing, excluded from ground truth, and reported at build time. Post-wave census matched the sealed pre-wave census in both passes: 0 unexplained additions, 0 sealed timelines missing, 12/12 and 11/11 trial-created timelines present.
deviations: pass 1 ran with the operator's global AGENTS.md in trial context (--keep-agents); see passes.pass1.deviation. Pass 2 is the clean control; both are published, neither was rewritten.

tenancy: both passes shared the local Splash engine with this operator session (the operator session was idle during pass 2's trials). Disclosed rather than avoided; the published 17g wave was also tenancy-disclosed.

the smoke trial (T1r1, scratch out-dir) ran before pass 1 against the pass-1 project. T1 is read-only and the post-run timeline census matched the sealed ground truth exactly, so no pre-state contamination.
no harness drift: opencode v2.3.0 for all 42 sessions; grader selftest 58/58 green immediately before each grading.
protocol: grading from independent read-backs only (predicates from grader_selftest.py, 58/58 green immediately before each grading); T8 graded from the driver's in-trial snapshot at each session's end, post-wave comp reads kept as product-behavior data; claims maps operator-extracted from archived transcripts (regex drafts reviewed and discarded, never fed to the grader); missing claims fail closed; graders fail closed when the target timeline is absent (a None timeline_id silently reads the CURRENT timeline — caught mid-wave).
evidence: bench/resolve-agentic/results/baseline-2026-11-17h/ (README.md = pass-1 record incl. findings and reproduce commands) and results/baseline-2026-11-17h2/ (README.md = pass-2 record); both trees gitignored by the wave-hygiene rule, published records are results-<wave>.json; plan and errata: bench/resolve-agentic/PLAN-baseline-2026-11-17h.md

trials_backfill.rule: per-trial scalars copied from the wave's driver log; `verified` is the grader verdict, never the driver ok flag; unmeasurable verdicts are kept as explicit nulls; grader notes/why and claim quotes are not copied
